caption: The TNT duplicator: 86 lit TNT a minute, standing right on the ground, and no explosion ever touches it. Each TNT is thrown away at 1 block per tick and explodes on the ground 9 to 30 blocks off, where it breaks blocks, beyond the 7 blocks a blast reaches. It is two catalog parts: the 16-block duplicator engine, which makes one TNT each time its piston loses power for a moment, and a 6-block clock from the clock catalog (period 14 ticks) whose redstone block holds that piston and steps away for 4 ticks of every 14. Detail: robust over every kick angle on both grounds on redsim (and 64 runs with every TNT its own kick), 16 builds in the game; a period-10 clock gives 120 a minute but lands blasts 5.3 blocks away and fails about 1 game build in 30.

Every lit TNT falls straight down from one point and explodes at exactly the same spot in the air, 10 blocks under the machine, bit for bit, 30 a minute (for tree farms and anything else that needs every blast at one known place below): a small clock lets the duplicator make one TNT every 40 ticks and throw it into fence posts that stop it over a little water channel; the current pushes it against an observer (that cancels the random sideways kick every TNT gets when it is lit) onto an iron trapdoor, and the next TNT's push opens the trapdoor, so it falls straight down and explodes at the end of its fuse. Stand it 23 blocks up: it then explodes 13 blocks above the ground, in the air.

Every lit TNT explodes at exactly the same point in the air, bit for bit, 22 a minute, and breaks nothing of the machine, in a build only 4 blocks wide: a small clock lets the duplicator make one TNT every 54 ticks and throw it into fence posts that stop it over a little water channel; the current pushes it against a fence post standing on a slime block (that cancels the random sideways kick every TNT gets when it is lit), and the next TNT's push, carried by a line of observers, makes a piston under the slime launch it straight up, so it explodes at the top of its flight, more than 7 blocks from anything a blast could break. The precise TNT duplicator for builds that need every TNT at one known spot in the air; the fast one is tnt-clocked-22b.

A TNT dropper with an on/off lever: every lit TNT falls straight down and explodes at exactly the same point in the air, 9 blocks under the machine, 30 a minute while the lever is on. Each TNT is released by its own hopper timer (a dropper pushes one item into a ring of 11 hoppers, whose comparator opens the trapdoor 53 ticks later), so turning the lever off never leaves a TNT stuck in the water. Build it 23 blocks above the ground so the TNT explodes in mid-air.

A TNT launcher with an on/off lever: every lit TNT is thrown up and explodes at exactly the same point in the air, 22 a minute while the lever is on, and nothing of the machine breaks. A hopper timer launches each TNT 63 ticks after it is lit, so turning the lever off never leaves a TNT on the launcher. It works standing right on the ground.

One button press, one lit TNT: however long the button stays pressed, the duplicator lights exactly one TNT, when the button pops back out. A redstone torch holds the engine's sticky piston; the button powers the stone under the piston and darkens the torch, and at the release the stone goes quiet 2 ticks before the torch lights again, so the piston drops and comes back exactly once. It works standing right on the ground.

The fastest TNT duplicator, with an on/off lever: 200 lit TNT a minute while the lever is on, and it stops within 2 ticks when you turn it off. A redstone torch holds the engine's sticky piston while the lever is off; turning the lever on darkens the torch and the 16-block engine runs by itself, its own redstone block powering the piston again every 6 ticks. Build it 6 blocks above the ground: the TNT explodes under it, and from that height no blast reaches the machine.
